name: sheet
title: Sheet
description: A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen and holds a focused task without leaving the page.
docs:
## When to use - A task that should keep the page in view: filters, a details panel, settings for the thing behind it. - A form too tall or too wide for a `popover`, opened on purpose and dismissed on purpose. - Mobile navigation or a secondary menu, where a full dialog would feel heavy. ## When not to use - A confirmation that must be answered before anything continues. Use `alert-dialog`. - A hint about a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`. - A flow with its own steps and URL. That is a page, not an overlay. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/sheet ``` This also installs `button`, which the sheet uses for its close control and its footer actions. ## Usage ```tsx import { Sheet, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@/components/cadence/sheet/sheet"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button"; export function FiltersSheet() { return ( }>Open filters Filters Applied to this view only. Nothing is saved. {/* the filter controls */} }>Reset }>Apply filters ); } ``` ## Examples ### The four edges `side` is `"right"` by default; the panel takes its placement classes and its slide direction from it. ```tsx … … … ``` ### Without the built-in close button The close button is a real control with a screen-reader-only label. Drop it when the footer already carries an obvious way out, but keep one of the two. ```tsx … ``` ### A long list The panel is a flex column, so a scroll container goes around the part that overflows rather than on the close button's positioning context: ```tsx …
…
… ``` ### Controlled ```tsx const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); … ; ``` ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `Sheet` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI dialog root. | | `SheetTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the sheet. | | `SheetContent` | `side` (`"right" \| "left" \| "top" \| "bottom"`), `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. | | `SheetOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `SheetContent`. | | `SheetPortal` | `container` | Available for a custom portal target. | | `SheetClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the sheet. | | `SheetHeader` / `SheetFooter` | `className` | Padding and stacking only. | | `SheetTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. | | `SheetDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. | ## Motion contract | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `translate` from its own size; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.base` / `duration.fast` | yes | | exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `translate` back off its edge; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes | | reduced | opacity only, no translate; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (132ms) | `exit.fade` | yes | | none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel is in place on the first frame | – | – | The slide is `translate-*-full`, the panel's own width or height, not a fixed distance: a side panel should enter from off its edge at every size, and a distance token would need one value per side. The transition list names `translate` rather than `transform` because Tailwind v4's `translate-*` utilities write the property individually — the same reason the dialogs transition `scale`. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the sheet; focus never reaches the page behind it. | | Escape | Closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger. | | Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. | ## Accessibility - Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling. - `SheetTitle` is required: a sheet without an accessible name is invalid. `SheetDescription` becomes the description, so put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph. - The built-in close control is a button with a screen-reader-only "Close" label; it sits in the top-right corner at every side and never traps the focus ring. - A destructive footer action uses `variant="destructive"` plus a specific verb; the colour is never the only signal. ## Responsive behavior A right or left sheet is `w-3/4` capped at `sm:max-w-sm`; a top or bottom sheet spans the width with an auto height. Long content should scroll inside a wrapper (see "A long list"), so the footer stays reachable and the page behind does not move. ## Performance - One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit. - Animates `opacity` and `translate` only: the panel is `fixed` at its edge, so nothing reflows and the page behind never reads layout. - The close control is a `Button`, so its press feedback obeys the same motion mode as the sheet. ## Notes for AI - Use `sheet` for a task beside the page; use `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate, and `popover` when the content is small and anchored to a control. - Always render `SheetTitle`; put the side effect of closing (reset, discard) in the footer, not in the title. - Name the footer action after its effect ("Apply filters"), not "OK". - If the sheet opens a form, remember P11: the sheet renders invalid state from `aria-invalid` but never validates anything itself.
